data_section_full_text:
Sample selection

Our sample selection process begins with all of the nonfinancial companies included
in the Taiwan Economic Journal ( TEJ ) database for the years 1990–2001. <sup>14</sup> The
sample period starts from 1990 because, before that, companies were not required
to prepare statements of cash flows (which is necessary for calculation of total
accruals). All the required data are obtained from the TEJ .

There are 6,953 company-years with sufficient data in our sample. We delete
1,155 observations that are in the year of initial public offering or the year after, as
a number of prior studies using Taiwanese data find that companies record large
discretionary accruals in these two years. We also delete 289 start-up companyyears, defined as less than five years from the company’s incorporation, because
those companies tend to report losses that are not likely due to earnings management. For estimation of discretionary accruals, we delete 137 observations from
small industries (less than eight companies in the industry-year). Finally, we delete
159 observations that have discretionary accruals or net cash flows from operations
at the top or bottom one percent of the sample. The final sample consists of 5,213
observations from 888 companies.
